code.originalText: Six-week review with a trial without catheter and a geriatric assessment

text.paragraph: Six-week review with a trial without catheter and a geriatric assessment. [S]

Mr. Tagore returns six weeks after the catheter was placed and two weeks after a catheter-associated urinary tract infection, treated with ceftriaxone and then cefpodoxime for 7 days in all, which he finished eight days ago. The urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to cephalosporins and the blood cultures had no growth. He has had no fever since the third day of treatment. The catheter was removed at seven this morning; he has passed only small amounts twice, about 40 mL each time, and feels full and uncomfortable. He takes tamsulosin at bedtime and finasteride daily without dizziness, breast tenderness, or falls, although he once felt unsteady getting up at night before the catheter was placed. He brought his herbal preparation for the pharmacist. He wants to understand what comes next if the trial fails. [S]

list.item:
Chronic urinary retention; first trial without catheter failed (R33.8). Bladder scan 420 mL after two small voids: the trial without catheter has failed after six weeks of tamsulosin, as it often does in chronic retention. Creatinine 1.16 mg/dL (eGFR 64). [S]
Catheter replaced today.
Continue tamsulosin and finasteride.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia with refractory retention (N40.1). With retention that has not responded to an alpha-blocker, Dr. Marsh-Okoro recommends an operation, by telephone today. Options for an 85 mL prostate were explained: laser enucleation (HoLEP), the preferred choice, under spinal or general anesthesia, with a short stay and a high chance of voiding again; transurethral resection or simple prostatectomy as alternatives; and prostatic artery embolization by an interventional radiologist under local anesthesia, a less invasive option with lower and less durable success. Prostatic urethral lift and water vapor therapy are less suitable at this size, with a median lobe, and in retention. The alternatives to any procedure are a long-term catheter (urethral or suprapubic) or a second trial without catheter after three to six months of finasteride. [S]
Written information on each option given to him.
He wants time to think and to talk with his family; decision visit in four weeks.

Mild frailty (R54). Clinical Frailty Scale 5 with a slow gait; cognition normal. Age, frailty, and a recent infection raise his risk of delirium after anesthesia; his normal cognition and good support lower it. [S]
Walking and chair-stand exercises daily; protein at each meal.
Fall precautions with bedtime tamsulosin: rise slowly, sit to pass urine at night, night light.

Catheter-associated urinary tract infection, resolved (T83.511A). Treated for 7 days; well, with no fever since the third day of treatment. [S]
No further antibiotics; no urine testing without symptoms.
